Jack Heart, 2026-11-14: "this system should still not rule out the idea of evals just running locally on the client machine ... In that case you get the keys that you have. I imagine there will be reasons long term where we'll want to have both rented compute and some sort of keys to access even further compute down the line but for now I don't think we need to do that". So hosted-model evals start with `etude eval FILE` on the client machine, reading the API key from that machine's environment; delivering keys to rented machines is deferred. EXP-66 keeps `etude eval` as play-here and lets an eval job seat checkpoints from other experiments, fetched to this machine from the source.
